text: The normal semester load for undergraduate B.Tech students is governed by the semester-wise curriculum matrix, typically ranging between 17 and 19.5 credits per regular semester.

In general a student has to register for the nominal load as per the semester-wise program curriculum. Overload/underload can only be permitted from third semester onwards. BTech students may be allowed to register up to a maximum of 21 credits from their third semester onwards by the concerned DUGC conveners on a case-to-case basis.

Underload can only be permitted from third semester onwards. BTech students may be allowed to register for a minimum of 15 credits from their third semester onwards by the concerned DUGC conveners on a case-to-case basis.
In the eighth regular semester, BTech students may be allowed to register up to a minimum of 9 credits by the concerned DUGC conveners subject to fulfilling all pending credit requirements.

To be eligible for the award of a BTech in Computer Science and Engineering degree, a candidate must earn at least 144 course credits (comprising 40.5 Institute Core, 4 Program Linked, 52 Program Core, 22.5 Program Elective, 15 Open Elective, and 10 Liberal Arts) plus 12 Non-Graded Core units, maintaining a minimum CGPA of 4.5.

Pre-requisites shall be defined only in terms of other course code(s). A precedent course defined as a prerequisite for a course must be cleared (obtaining a passing grade; non-F grade) before the dependent course can be registered.
A student shall be allowed to opt for a maximum of 6 credits from MOOC-based portals (such as NPTEL / SWAYAM) for considering against credit transfer during their entire B.Tech undergraduate program.
A 14-week or 42-hour MOOC/NPTEL course shall be considered equivalent to a full-semester course worth 3 credits of IIT Bhilai. Prior departmental DUGC approval is mandatory before enrolling.

The respective DUGC convener acts as instructor-in-charge for any approved MOOC-based course (using course code format CSL495). The proctored grade is displayed on the semester grade sheet and counted directly towards CGPA calculation.

A student at the end of the 5th semester can apply to register for BTech Honours or Minor specialization in another discipline. Eligibility requires a cumulative CGPA of 8.0 or above, no active backlogs, and successful completion of 24 additional credits beyond the normal 144 credits.
applies_to: Undergraduate B.Tech students at completion of Semester 5

text: If SGPA falls below 4.5 in any semester, the student will be placed on academic probation with a warning letter issued by the Dean of Academic Affairs (DoAA). A student on probation is prohibited from participating in off-campus extracurricular events.
A student will normally not be allowed to register and their academic program will be automatically terminated if their Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) falls below 4.0.
Students may add or drop courses using the academic registration system within 5 working days of the commencement of the regular semester, subject to approval by the DUGC convener.
applies_to: All registered students at the start of each semester

text: Course grade improvement examination can be carried out for a maximum of three courses where the student was awarded a grade of C or less and cumulative CGPA is less than or equal to 5.0, provided it does not increase normal semester load.
applies_to: Students with C or lower grade and CGPA <= 5.0

text: A student is required to maintain a minimum attendance of 75% in each registered course to be eligible to sit for the end-semester examination, unless granted medical dispensation by the Senate.
